summary: This section explains how companies can issue securities, which are financial instruments like shares. It sets different rules for public companies and private companies. Public companies can issue securities to the public, through private placement, or via rights and bonus issues. Private companies can issue them through rights and bonus issues or private placement.
points: A public company may issue securities to the public through a prospectus.
A public company may issue securities through private placement.
A public company may issue securities through a rights issue or a bonus issue.
A private company may issue securities through a rights issue or a bonus issue.
A private company may issue securities through private placement.
A public offer includes initial public offers, further public offers, or offers for sale by an existing shareholder.
example: Sunshine Pharma Limited is a public company that wants to raise money to build a new factory. To do this, the company decides to issue new shares to the general public by releasing an official document called a prospectus. Meanwhile, a smaller family business named Meera Textiles Private Limited also needs funds for new machinery. Since it is a private company, it cannot issue shares to the general public. Instead, Meera Textiles chooses to issue new shares through a rights issue to its current shareholders and also considers a private placement, strictly following the rules laid down in the Act.

terms.meaning: Financial instruments like shares or bonds issued by a company.
An official document inviting the public to buy securities.
A way of offering securities to a select group of people instead of the general public.
Offering new shares to existing shareholders first.

watch: Do not assume private companies can issue securities to the general public like public companies can.
